chunks: If you ask them: 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they will answer: 'The Mighty and All-knowing created them,'
ai.seo_question: Who do polytheists acknowledge as the Creator when asked about the heavens and the earth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (31:25) is often cited to demonstrate the innate recognition of Tawhid (monotheism) even among polytheists, who acknowledge Allah as the Creator but fail to extend that recognition to His Lordship and Authority. This distinction highlights the cognitive dissonance in idolatry, where the act of creation is accepted, yet the sovereignty of the Creator is denied. The verse serves as a rhetorical proof for the inevitability of resurrection, as the same Power that created the heavens and earth is fully capable of restoring life.
